chunks: From him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
"Shaving the head, other than during Hajj or Umrah, is a mutilation."
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on shaving the head if not for Hajj or Umrah?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) linking the act of shaving the head outside of Hajj or Umrah to the concept of *muthlah* (mutilation or disfigurement). This classification elevates the act from mere custom to a legal violation of altering Allah's creation, reflecting the Shia juristic view that ritual shaving is a specific act of worship (*ibadah*) whose performance outside its designated context constitutes an improper alteration of the body. The ruling underscores the importance of intentionality in physical acts of worship within Shia fiqh.
